headline: A rather important omission
dek: The President accuses the New York Times of leaving out, in an article about a lawsuit settled at his golf club in Bedminster, that the case did not involve him, and calls it fake news. Made neutral.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The failing New York Times wrote about the “settling of a sexual harassment suit brought years ago by a waitress at President Trump’s golf club in Bedminster, N.J.” What they fail to say is that it did not involve President Trump, a rather important omission. FAKE NEWS!!!
original.key: What they fail to say is that it did not involve President Trump, a rather important omission. FAKE NEWS!!!
original.context: Posted late on 10 November 2026 (Pacific time). The President quotes a New York Times article about the settlement of a lawsuit brought by a former employee of his golf club in Bedminster, New Jersey, and says the case did not involve him. Our versions are about the newspaper and the omission he points to, not about the case.

verification.note: Copied by the editor from truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 11 November 2026 (shown as Nov 10, 2026, 10:47 PM Pacific).

en: A recent New York Times article about the settlement of a lawsuit at one of my clubs did not make clear that, as I understand it, the case did not concern me personally.
I have asked the newspaper to clarify this. A free press is essential to our democracy, and so is accuracy.
fr: Un récent article du New York Times sur le règlement d’une plainte dans l’un de mes clubs n’a pas précisé que, selon moi, l’affaire ne me concernait pas personnellement.
J’ai demandé au journal de le préciser. Une presse libre est essentielle à notre démocratie, et l’exactitude l’est tout autant.
presidential.key: I have asked the newspaper to clarify this. A free press is essential to our democracy, and so is accuracy.

neuchatelois.hook: Une omission plutôt importante ! *Comme une montre sans l’aiguille des minutes.*
neuchatelois.hookEn: A rather important omission! *Like a watch without its minute hand.*
neuchatelois.short: Chez nous, une montre sans l’aiguille des minutes, ça donne l’heure. À peu près. *Un article sans le détail important, pareil.*
neuchatelois.shortEn: Round here a watch without a minute hand still tells the time. Roughly. *An article without the key detail, same thing.*
text: Le New York Times, ce journal en faillite, je le dis, a écrit sur une affaire réglée dans mon club de golf. Mais il a oublié de préciser que ça ne me concernait pas. Une omission plutôt importante. Fake news !

Chez nous, une montre sans l’aiguille des minutes, ça donne encore l’heure. À peu près. Un horloger ne la vendrait jamais. Un article sans le détail important, c’est pareil : on ne le livre pas, on le renvoie à l’atelier.
en: The New York Times, a failing paper, I say, wrote about a case settled at my golf club. But it forgot to say it didn’t involve me. A rather important omission. Fake news!

Round here, a watch without a minute hand still tells the time. Roughly. No watchmaker would ever sell it. An article without the key detail is the same: you don’t deliver it, you send it back to the workshop.
notes: Neuchâtel and its Jura mountains are the heart of Swiss watchmaking, where a watch is checked to the second before it leaves the workshop.

valaisan.hook: Une omission plutôt importante ! *Comme une raclette sans le fromage.*
valaisan.hookEn: A rather important omission! *Like a raclette without the cheese.*
valaisan.short: Chez nous, une raclette sans le fromage, ça s’appelle des patates. *Un article sans le détail important, pareil : des patates.*
valaisan.shortEn: Round here a raclette without the cheese is called potatoes. *An article without the key detail: potatoes.*
text: Adieu ! Le New York Times a écrit sur une affaire réglée dans mon club de golf, mais il a oublié de dire que ça ne me concernait pas, à ce que je dis. Une omission plutôt importante. Fake news !

Chez nous, une raclette sans le fromage, ça s’appelle des patates. Et personne ne te remercie pour des patates. Un article sans le détail important, c’est pareil : des patates. Bon, avec un verre de fendant, ça passe mieux.
en: Adieu! The New York Times wrote about a case settled at my golf club, but forgot to say it didn’t involve me, or so I say. A rather important omission. Fake news!

Round here, a raclette without the cheese is called potatoes. And nobody thanks you for potatoes. An article without the key detail is the same: potatoes. Well, with a glass of Fendant it goes down better.
notes: Raclette, cheese melted by the fire and scraped onto boiled potatoes, comes from Valais; Fendant is the Valais name for the Chasselas white wine.

en: Switzerland takes note that the President and the New York Times disagree about what the article should have said.

We would suggest a quiet solution: the newspaper adds one sentence, the President removes three exclamation marks, and everyone meets in Geneva over a fondue. Neutrality is mostly a matter of punctuation.
fr: La Suisse prend acte que le Président et le New York Times ne sont pas d’accord sur ce que l’article aurait dû dire.

Nous suggérons une solution discrète : le journal ajoute une phrase, le Président retire trois points d’exclamation, et tout le monde se retrouve à Genève autour d’une fondue. La neutralité est surtout une affaire de ponctuation.
neutral.key: The newspaper adds one sentence, the President removes three exclamation marks, and everyone meets in Geneva over a fondue.
neutral.keyFr: Le journal ajoute une phrase, le Président retire trois points d’exclamation, et tout le monde se retrouve à Genève autour d’une fondue.
